name: paged
description:
The regression test for the sensor list being fetched once. LimaCharlie pages GET /v1/sensors/{oid} with an opaque continuation token: the response carries `continuation_token` and the next request sends it back under the same query-parameter name, ending when it comes back absent, null, or empty (refractionPOINT/python-limacharlie Organization.list_sensors, refractionPOINT/go-limacharlie sensor.go rawSensorListPage).

Three pages, one sensor each, and each page route matches on the token that the PREVIOUS page returned -- so a walk that failed to send the token, or sent a stale one, starves on route 2 rather than quietly passing. Page 3 returns an empty-string token, the falsy spelling of 'no more'. request_count pins the walk at exactly four calls (one exchange, three pages): a script that treated "" as truthy would send it, fall through to the page-1 route again, and both re-import lc-page-1 (failing unique_ids) and make a fifth request. Every page route is when_exhausted:error, so no request may repeat. The sensors from pages 2 and 3 are asserted by id: a single-page walk imports only lc-page-1 and this scenario fails on the other two.

requests_absent pins is_compressed off. Sending it makes LimaCharlie return `sensors` as a base64-encoded gzip blob rather than a JSON array, which this script does not decode.

Page 2's sensor carries an ext_ip, asserted as a custom attribute and absent from ipAddresses.

namespaced_ids is skipped: id=sid is the bare LimaCharlie sensor UUID, which is globally unique on shape, so two organizations cannot collide.
